title: “Thou turnest man to destruction” — the Greek has “Turn not man back to humiliation”
summary: The KJV of Psalm 90:3 states that God turns man to destruction and says “Return”. Brenton’s Greek of the first clause is a prohibition with a negative, and the second clause is a question.
text: KJV Psalms 90:3: “Thou turnest man to destruction; and sayest, Return, ye children of men.” Hebrew (WLC) 90:3: תָּשֵׁ֣ב אֱ֭נֹושׁ עַד־דַּכָּ֑א וַ֝תֹּ֗אמֶר. The Greek begins with μή and a verb in the form of a request, so it asks that man not be turned back; and it ends with a question mark where the KJV has a full stop. The KJV states something God does; the Greek, as Brenton’s English prints it, asks him not to do it.
